Criteria

/kry-TEER-ee-uh/ - the stress falls on TEER · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Criteria means the standards by which something is judged.

The kite festival publishes its criteria in four languages: lift, line control, originality, and survival of the final gust.

Worked Example

Two essays about the harbor tied for the prize until the judges reread their own criteria: clarity, evidence, and grace of expression carried stated weights, and the flashier essay, rescored on all three with those weights, finished second by a point.

Criteria is the word for those standards because criteria means exactly that — the yardsticks a judgment leans on. Note the grammar the SAT loves: criteria is plural. One standard is a criterion; the panel's three criteria form its whole rulebook.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

yardsticks: the informal image for the same standards

touchstones: the tests a thing must pass to count as genuine

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

whims: judgments that change with the judge's mood

guesswork: scoring with no standards at all

Where it sits · how binding the standards are — hunches → criteria → commandments

hunches vs. criteria: Hunches judge by feel — nothing written, nothing you could appeal to.

commandments vs. criteria: Commandments go further than criteria — criteria guide a judgment that still has to be made; commandments end the judging before it starts.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cri-

Root — cri-: to judge, decide (Greek krinein)

Suffix — -teria

Suffix — -teria: means of judging (Greek -tērion; plural -tēria)

Put it together

Put it together: Cri- (to judge) + -teria (means of judging, in the plural) = the instruments judging is done with. Greek kritērion named the judge's test; English borrowed the plural whole, which is why one test is a criterion and the panel's list is criteria — the -a ending is Greek plural, not a typo.

Use the root in a new word: critic

Use the root in a new word: critic: A critic is literally a judger — the same Greek krinein weighing plays and restaurants today.

Word Choice

neutral / academic

Criteria is the word for stated, checkable standards — admissions, contests, diagnoses. Keep the number straight: one criterion, several criteria; 'a criteria' costs credibility in exactly the essays that get read closely. Where no standards are published, you're dealing with its antonyms — whims and guesswork.
